latest_teacher_action.diagnosis: The first prompt preserved truck count and the behind relation, but it was too loose for hard material binding and for keeping all three groups distinctly countable in one frame. The pigs were likely not rendered as clearly glass or as four separate pigs, the trucks were only weakly read as wooden, and the cows were not emphasized enough as a visible six-object group, causing cow omission or undercount. The plan relied on general clarity language instead of explicit per-group layout and per-object material cues.
expected_improvement: Stronger attribute binding should make each truck read as wooden and each pig read as glass.
Explicit row-based layout with left-to-right separations should improve counting for the four pigs and six cows.
A dedicated visible cow row should increase cow presence and reduce missing-object failure while preserving their white color.
Maintaining the already successful behind relation and truck count should keep passed constraints stable.
preserve_constraints: The trucks are behind the pigs.

previous_plan_error.details: The previous prompt grouped the cows only as a separate visible group and described the pigs/trucks in broad terms. It did not force a simple countable composition for all fourteen objects or strongly bind material appearance to each target object. That left the generator room to stylize pigs as non-glass, trucks as non-wooden, and to omit or merge cows.

latest_teacher_action.regeneration_strategy: Use a simple wide studio-style composition with three clearly separated horizontal bands or rows: four glass pigs in the front row, four wooden trucks directly behind them in a second row, and six white cows in a third separate row. Make every instance fully visible, evenly spaced, and similar in size so the counts are easy to verify. Add explicit material descriptors tied only to trucks and pigs, and add negative clauses against extra or merged instances.
regression_risks: Increasing emphasis on cows could accidentally change the passed truck-behind-pig relation unless the second row is stated explicitly.
Strong material wording for pigs and trucks could cause unusual stylization that merges instances unless spacing and full visibility are also enforced.
Adding many objects may invite extras or partial duplicates unless exact counts and no-extras language remain explicit.
repair_constraints: All 4 trucks must be clearly wooden trucks, with visible wood material appearance.
Show exactly 4 pigs, as 4 separate fully visible pigs.
All 4 pigs must be clearly glass pigs, with transparent glass appearance.
Show exactly 6 cows, as 6 separate fully visible cows.
Ensure cows are clearly present and easy to detect as cows.
Keep the trucks behind the pigs.
Do not include any extra trucks, pigs, or cows.
latest_teacher_action.retry_prompt: Create a clear wide studio-style image containing exactly three separated groups. In the front row, show exactly four glass pigs, each a complete pig, fully visible, transparent glass, and clearly separated left to right so all four are easy to count. Directly behind that front row, show exactly four wooden trucks, each a complete truck, fully visible, clearly made of wood, and aligned behind the pigs so the trucks are unmistakably behind the pigs. In a third separate row, show exactly six white cows, each a complete cow, fully visible, clearly separated left to right, and easy to count. Keep all fourteen objects unobstructed, not touching, not overlapping, and entirely inside the frame. Do not include any extra trucks, extra pigs, extra cows, duplicate animals, or other prominent objects.

skill_revision.reason: Keep the same skill set, but apply it more concretely: stronger per-object material binding for wooden trucks and glass pigs, stricter exact-count wording for pigs and cows, and a simpler explicit row layout to improve object presence and countability.

Add explicit material descriptors tied only to trucks and pigs, and add negative clauses against extra or merged instances.
